text: The book cites f(x) = e^(−1/x²) (with f(0) = 0) as a function that is C∞ but not analytic at 0. Why is it not analytic there?
choices: Because it is discontinuous at x = 0.
Because it fails to be differentiable at x = 0.
Because its derivatives at 0 exist only up to some finite order.
Because all of its derivatives at 0 are 0, so its Taylor series is identically 0, yet f(x) ≠ 0 for x ≠ 0 — the series does not equal f in any neighborhood.
explanation: Analyticity means a function equals its Taylor series near the point. For e^(−1/x²) every derivative at 0 vanishes, so its Taylor series is the zero series, which cannot equal the nonzero function for x ≠ 0. The book stresses the function is smooth (C∞), infinitely differentiable and continuous, so options 0, 1, and 2 all contradict that; the only obstruction is the Taylor-series mismatch.
